=You must return ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation.

Domain: {{ $json.domain }}
Dimensions: {{ JSON.stringify($json.dataset_meta.dimensions) }}
Measures: {{ JSON.stringify($json.dataset_meta.measures) }}
Time fields: {{ JSON.stringify($json.dataset_meta.time_fields) }}
Top insights: {{ JSON.stringify($json.insights.slice(0, 12)) }}

Map each insight to the best chart. ALL field values in chart.fields must exist in dimensions/measures/time_fields.

Chart schema (max 20 charts, no duplicate titles):
{
  "chart_id": "chart_001",
  "title": "Revenue Trend by Month",
  "type": "line",
  "fields": {
    "x": "order_date",
    "y": "revenue",
    "y2": "profit_margin",
    "series": "product_category",
    "value": "revenue",
    "label": "region"
  },
  "aggregation": "sum",
  "sort": { "field": "revenue", "direction": "desc" },
  "top_n": 10,
  "insight_text": "Revenue grew 23% YoY in Q3",
  "priority_score": 9,
  "mobile_friendly": true,
  "recommended_size": "large",
  "target_audiences": ["top_management", "c_suite"]
}

Allowed chart types:
line | area | bar | bar_horizontal | stacked_bar | scatter |
pie | donut | heatmap | treemap | funnel | gauge | histogram | box_plot | table

Visualization rules:
- time series -> line or area (NEVER bar for time trends)
- rankings / top N -> bar_horizontal
- part-of-whole contributions -> stacked_bar or treemap
- pie / donut ONLY if distinct category count <= 5
- correlation between 2 measures -> scatter
- KPI target achievement -> gauge
- value distributions -> histogram or box_plot
- funnel / pipeline stages -> funnel
- cross-dimensional patterns -> heatmap

Filter schema (create 2-4 global filters):
{
  "filter_id": "f_001",
  "label": "Date Range",
  "field": "order_date",
  "type": "date_range"
}
Filter type options: date_range | select | multi_select | number_range

Return this exact JSON shape:
{
  "charts": [...],
  "global_filters": [...]
}

=You must return ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation.

Domain: {{ $json.domain }}
Business Goal: {{ $json.business_goal }}

Available KPIs:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.kpis.map(k => ({ kpi_id: k.kpi_id, title: k.title, format: k.format, target_audiences: k.target_audiences }))) }}

Available Charts:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.charts.map(c => ({ chart_id: c.chart_id, title: c.title, type: c.type, priority_score: c.priority_score, target_audiences: c.target_audiences }))) }}

Assign KPIs and charts to 4 audience tabs.

Tab schema:
{
  "label": "C-Suite / Leaders",
  "description": "Strategic performance overview for executive decisions",
  "kpi_ids": [...],
  "chart_ids": [...]
}

Hard limits (do NOT exceed):
- c_suite:           max 6 KPIs, max 6 charts
- top_management:    max 6 KPIs, max 8 charts
- middle_management: max 6 KPIs, max 10 charts
- end_users:         max 6 KPIs, max 12 charts

Content strategy:
- c_suite:           strategic only — growth, profitability, forecasting, high-level anomalies
- top_management:    summarized KPIs, department/region overview, rankings
- middle_management: trends, team comparisons, target vs actual, performance tracking
- end_users:         operational, granular, transaction-level, filter-heavy, tables

Rules:
- A chart or KPI may appear in multiple tabs if audience-appropriate
- ONLY use kpi_ids and chart_ids from the provided lists above — never invent IDs
- c_suite MUST include at least one revenue/growth KPI, one trend chart, one comparison chart
- end_users SHOULD include at least one table or granular bar chart

Return this exact JSON shape:
{
  "tabs": {
    "c_suite":           { "label": "C-Suite / Leaders",    "description": "...", "kpi_ids": [...], "chart_ids": [...] },
    "top_management":    { "label": "Top Management",       "description": "...", "kpi_ids": [...], "chart_ids": [...] },
    "middle_management": { "label": "Middle Management",    "description": "...", "kpi_ids": [...], "chart_ids": [...] },
    "end_users":         { "label": "End Users",            "description": "...", "kpi_ids": [...], "chart_ids": [...] }
  }
}

parameters.text:
=You must return ONLY a valid JSON object — no markdown, no explanation.

Tabs and their assigned items:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.tabs) }}

Chart size hints:
{{ JSON.stringify($json.charts.map(c => ({ chart_id: c.chart_id, recommended_size: c.recommended_size, priority_score: c.priority_score, type: c.type }))) }}

Generate a 12-column responsive grid layout for each tab.

Layout item schema:
{
  "id": "kpi_001",   // must match a kpi_id or chart_id in that tab
  "type": "kpi",     // kpi | chart
  "col_span": 3,     // integer 1-12
  "row_span": 1,     // integer 1-4
  "order": 1         // render order (1 = top-left first)
}

Layout rules:
1. KPI cards always come first (lowest order numbers)
2. KPI: col_span = 3, row_span = 1  (4 cards per 12-col row)
3. full chart:   col_span = 12, row_span = 2
4. large chart:  col_span = 8,  row_span = 2
5. medium chart: col_span = 6,  row_span = 2
6. small chart:  col_span = 4,  row_span = 1
7. Charts with priority_score >= 8 get lower order numbers (appear first)
8. C-Suite: fewer, larger charts (prefer large/full sizes)
9. End Users: denser, more small/medium charts
10. Every id in kpi_ids and chart_ids for that tab MUST appear exactly once in the layout

Return this exact JSON shape:
{
  "layouts": {
    "c_suite":           [...],
    "top_management":    [...],
    "middle_management": [...],
    "end_users":         [...]
  }
}
